answer: A memory-hard pebbling protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to compute sequential state proofs across a directed graph trellis. Before interacting at a protocol inlet, each node must register dynamic memory allocations on a shared validator atlas. An attacker incurs a verifiable, non-fungible cost of dedicated physical RAM per identity. However, this mechanism penalizes low-spec edge agents and incentivizes hardware pooling in industrial data centers.
